parsed.summary: Assume ν > 0 and that (u, p, f, K) satisfies the bundled CandidateProperties: smooth periodic fields on the pre-singular domain, zero initial velocity, divergence-free, solving Navier–Stokes with force f on 0<t<1, and speed unbounded at t=1. Under these assumptions the Lean theorem proves four energy conclusions: ‖f(t)‖_{L²} is interval-integrable on [0,1]; the dissipation is integrable on [0,1); for every T∈[0,1), ‖u(T)‖² + 2ν∫₀ᵀ D ≤ (∫₀ᵀ‖f‖)²; and the analogous total bound 2ν∫_{[0,1)} D ≤ (∫₀¹‖f‖)² holds. The excerpt only says Lemma 10.4 gives 'global energy and integrated dissipation bounds for the localized fields directly from their equation'. That is consistent with this declaration, but the exact statement is not in the excerpt. The main caveat is that l2Norm, l2Sq, dissipation, the domain helpers and SpeedUnboundedAtOne are not shown, so the normalisations and integration domain cannot be checked.

glossary.plain: Bundle of hypotheses on (ν,u,p,f,K): u, p smooth on the pre-singular domain and f smooth everywhere; unit spatial periodicity (u, p for t∈[0,1), f for t≥0); spatial supports inside a compact K in the open fundamental cube; u(0,·)=0; f vanishes for t≤0 and has compact future time support; div u=0 on [0,1); NS residual = f on (0,1); speed unbounded at t=1.
glossary.standard_concept: Properties of the constructed periodic blow-up candidate (smooth forced NS solution on [0,1) with zero data)
glossary.note: Helper definitions (preSingularDomain, UnitSpatialPeriodsOn, fundamentalCube/Interior, navierStokesResidual, SpeedUnboundedAtOne, CompactFutureTimeSupport) are not shown.

glossary.standard_concept: Cumulative L¹_t L²_x norm of the force
glossary.note: Depends on the unshown l2Norm; the junk value 0 for a non-integrable integrand is excluded because integrability is the first conjunct.

glossary.plain: Maps SpaceTime → ℝ³ and SpaceTime → ℝ

lean_claims.plain: For ν>0 and any u, f, p, K satisfying CandidateProperties ν u p f K, the following four conclusions hold: (i) t ↦ ‖f(t)‖_{L²} is interval-integrable on [0,1]; (ii) t ↦ dissipation u t is Lebesgue-integrable on [0,1); (iii) for every T∈[0,1), ‖u(T)‖²_{L²} + 2ν∫₀ᵀ dissipation u ≤ (∫₀ᵀ‖f‖_{L²})²; (iv) 2ν∫_{[0,1)} dissipation u ≤ (∫₀¹‖f‖_{L²})².

paper_claims.plain: Global energy and integrated dissipation bounds for the localized fields, derived directly from their equation (exact statement not in excerpt).

coverage.why: The only paper description (energy and integrated dissipation bounds) matches the Lean conclusions. Exact constants and form are not in the excerpt, so this is a tentative match.

flags.explanation: l2Norm, l2Sq and dissipation are not visible. The meaning depends on two things: whether they integrate over the fundamental cube (rather than all of ℝ³, which for periodic fields would be infinite or a junk value), and whether dissipation = ‖∇u‖² rather than ½‖∇u‖². The inequality ‖u(T)‖² + 2ν∫‖∇u‖² ≤ (∫‖f‖)² is the standard sharp consequence of ½d/dt‖u‖² + ν‖∇u‖² = ⟨f,u⟩, so the constants are consistent if dissipation = ‖∇u‖² over the cube.
flags.probe_idea: #print l2Sq; #print l2Norm; #print dissipation — check integration over fundamentalCube and dissipation u t = ∫_cube ‖∇ₓu(t,x)‖².

flags.explanation: The hypothesis bundles assumptions not needed for an energy estimate, such as speed_unbounded and periodicity. Extra hypotheses weaken the theorem. They are faithful to the paper's setting of a specific candidate, but they also make the result vacuous if no candidate exists; vacuity is not settled here.
flags.probe_idea: Exhibit or reference a theorem constructing some (u,p,f,K) with CandidateProperties ν u p f K.
